Date: Tue, 14 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Customer request: regional-only model binding (Acme Health) — please advise

Hi Lauren — forwarding Acme's ask from this morning. Short version: Acme Health is running PHI workflows and is refusing any fallback that would route inference outside the EU or to a different model family. They specifically want: (1) all inference pinned to the redwood-privacy-v1 model deployed in eu-west-1, (2) no automatic fallback to other model variants or regions under any capacity or degradation event, and (3) audit logging retained for 7 years.

They flagged regulatory concerns (GDPR + healthcare regulator) and say their legal team will not sign off unless we can provide a hard guarantee on routing + a BAA. I attached the customer's request packet and their SOC2 checklist for review.

Attachments: acme_request.pdf (customer letter), acme_soc2_request.xlsx

Can product + infra + security weigh in on feasibility asap? Acme is asking for a written answer by Friday. If we can't meet their ask exactly, we need a clear escalation path and a proposed mitigation to present.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Customer request: regional-only model binding (Acme Health) — please advise

Lauren / team — reading this through. Short technical note: a strict "no-fallback" + single-region bind is technically possible but operationally risky at scale. Key points: 

- Capacity: if eu-west-1 capacity for redwood-privacy-v1 is saturated or experiences degraded kernels (OOMs, driver hangs), requests will queue or fail; we currently rely on fallback pools to preserve availability.
- SLAs: removing fallback removes many of our graceful-degradation guarantees and will raise per-token cost due to forced overprovisioning; we would need a dedicated capacity commit or a hard reservation for this customer.
- Emergency runbook: we can implement a workflow where, during capacity emergencies, requests are queued and a documented manual escalation path is used to enable a temporary approved exception, but that requires legal/CS signoff and on-call commitments.

I drafted a suggested redline to our routing policy that defines a constrained exception path (attached). It includes an "isolated-exception" flag that: (a) pins model+region, (b) enforces strict KV cache segregation, (c) triggers a high-priority capacity allocation process, and (d) prohibits automatic cross-region fallback without explicit CTO approval.

See attached: proposed-routing-policy-redline.txt

Happy to run numbers on what commit would be needed to guarantee throughput for the customer's projected QPS. If the commercial team can secure a committed monthly reservation, the operational burden is manageable.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Inference Infrastructure

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 15 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Customer request: regional-only model binding (Acme Health) — please advise

Lauren / team — flagged several items after initial review of Acme's packet. High level: security will not recommend a permanent no-fallback exception without contractual and technical mitigations. Requirements we need fulfilled before recommending approval: 

1) Signed BAA and an explicit appendix in the contract that documents the "routing exception" and the operational consequences (queueing, potential failed requests, manual escalation path).
2) KMS integration: customer-managed keys preferred for encryption at rest for inference artifacts; we must document key rotation and access procedures.
3) Audit and retention: confirm that we can retain request-level logs for 7 years in EU-only storage (remove any cross-region replication).
4) SOC2 evidence: provide the customer's SOC2 items requested in their spreadsheet; I reviewed and attached a filled checklist with gaps noted.

We can propose a compromise: allow a tightly-scoped exception that pins model+region but requires (a) a committed capacity reservation, (b) a short-circuit manual failover runbook (manual permission to enable a controlled fallback for 30 minutes only, requiring VP approval), and (c) an incident compensation credit if we trigger the manual path. That gives us operational options while keeping the customer's controls. I realize Acme said they "refuse" fallback — if that's non-negotiable, we should escalate to Legal & GTM leadership to weigh commercial impact.

Attachment: security_checklist_filled.pdf

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
